assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle of the cell (P granules, nucleoli, multivalent-interaction condensates) is a genuinely new physical-chemical concept of molecular organisation. It recasts intracellular compartmentation in terms of phase behaviour, multivalency and thermodynamics, and has reshaped cell biology, neurodegeneration and amyloid research, close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the founding observation of liquid-like P granules in 2009; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction physical-chemical framework (2012). Pappu and Mittag are strong contributors but the three-person set captures the conceptual origin and the quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly reproduced across many systems and widely adopted. Mature enough in concept, though the field is still debating how general and functionally important condensates are in vivo.
uncertainties: Ongoing debate over whether many in vitro condensates reflect physiological function.
Credit among Rosen, Pappu, Mittag and others for the physical framework could be disputed.
Fit as a chemistry rather than physiology/medicine prize may be questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and colloid-chemistry solution to delivering nucleic acids, enabling siRNA therapy and mRNA vaccines at global scale. Pairing lipid phase behaviour and pKa-tuned ionizable lipids with microfluidic assembly is physical chemistry with enormous impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope developed the lipid-nanoparticle formation and ionizable-lipid concepts and the microfluidic process; Anderson and Langer led lipid discovery and screening for RNA delivery; MacLachlan and Madden contributed to early clinical formulations. The allocation is crowded and contested, and I choose the three I judge most decisive.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at very large scale, so mature and timely, though the 2023 medicine prize for mRNA modifications recognised part of the same translation.
uncertainties: Attribution is crowded across academic and industrial inventors, with patent disputes.
Overlap with the 2023 medicine prize may weigh against recognition.
Which lipid chemistry was decisive is partly unresolved to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape and funnel theory resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave protein folding a statistical-thermodynamic foundation, with hydrophobic-collapse and frustration concepts that connect directly to self-assembly. It is among the most conceptually influential physical-chemistry contributions to biology.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed the funnel and minimal-frustration framework; Dill articulated the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model view. Fersht contributed decisive experimental mapping, which could argue for a different configuration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation, including AlphaFold-era renewal of interest, so recognition is not premature; the question is whether it is overtaken by the 2024 structure-prediction prize.
uncertainties: Theory-versus-experiment split of credit with Fersht is unresolved.
The 2024 protein structure prediction prize may reduce appetite for another protein-folding award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells site-specifically incorporate non-canonical amino acids, a new concept of programming protein chemistry in living systems with broad tools in biophysics and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first in vivo orthogonal pairs, Wang was the key early developer, and Chin extended the approach to eukaryotes, quadruplet codons and engineered ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama are also significant.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used for over two decades; timely.
uncertainties: Ordering among Schultz, Chin and Wang may be contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through PROTACs and molecular glues is a new pharmacological modality built on chemical design of ternary-complex equilibria, now in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies created the first PROTACs, Ciulli contributed structure-guided design and VHL ligands, while Handa, Ito and Gray/Kim and Sakamoto matter for the glue and cereblon story. The credit is fragmented and I am unsure how to partition it.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing but not complete, so recognition could be somewhat early, though the concept is firmly established.
uncertainties: Approvals of PROTAC drugs are still pending.
Complex attribution between PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts chemical insight into precise single-nucleotide genome correction without double-strand breaks, a major chemical-biology invention with growing clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory invented cytosine and adenine base editors (Komor, Gaudelli as lead authors); a single-laureate configuration is defensible. Nishida and Kondo reported related deaminase fusions, so credit is not fully unambiguous. Prime editing, B048, would be a natural extension of the same recognition.
assessment.maturity: First clinical successes are emerging; the 2020 CRISPR chemistry prize shows the committee's openness but also overlap concern.
uncertainties: Credit for Nishida and Kondo may need weighing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near quantum accuracy at classical cost, enabling simulations of phase behaviour, water and interfaces that were previously out of reach. They broaden the reach of physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello introduced neural-network potentials, Bartók and Csányi Gaussian approximation potentials; von Lilienfeld and E also contributed. Parrinello is also credited in other candidates, so I weigh that overlap.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing but still evolving; the transferability and reliability of foundation models are active questions.
uncertainties: Overlap of Parrinello with Car-Parrinello and metadynamics candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography established how molecular organisation at surfaces and interfaces can be controlled and used, which is central to colloid and surface chemistry and to materials and biointerface science.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara demonstrated thiol-on-gold SAMs, Whitesides developed their systematic use and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers and Xia complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Decades old and thoroughly confirmed, so maturity is not an issue; the concern is that its moment may have passed.
uncertainties: Priority issues with Sagiv's earlier work.
Impact is diffuse, so I am unsure about a clear prize-sized discovery.
